r: **Alluri Sitarama Raju**; **1922-1924** (first raid **22 Aug 1922** – Raju shot **7 May 1924**)
Agency tracts of East Godavari and Visakhapatnam – the **Gudem hills**
The **Koya** tribe (with Konda Doras and Konda Reddis)
Armed tribal guerrilla war, **outside the Congress**; caused the British more trouble than the NCM in the region
**Raided police stations to seize British arms and used them against the British**
**Damanghat / Panjerighat** – the **first face-to-face battle** with the British army; officers **Scott Coward and Heiter** killed
**Peddagaddapalem** – **first defeat** of Raju's forces, a surprise attack by the **Malabar Special Police**; Raju escaped
Lieutenant **Gam Mallu Dora captured** – the first major setback
Paramilitary force – two companies brought in to end the rebellion
**Special Commissioner** appointed to suppress Raju – a civil (colonial) administrator
Officer in whose presence (on whose orders) Raju was shot
**Deputy Tahsildar of Gudem**, whose excesses sparked the revolt

0.x: The Malabar Special Police were used before the Assam Rifles.
Associates: **Gam Mallu Dora** (later an MP, 1952), **Gam Gantam Dora**, **Aggi Raju**; **Endu Padal**, a follower from Peddavalasa who wanted to become a muttadar.
First raid = **Chintapalli**; first battle = **Panjerighat**; force that ended it = **Assam Rifles**; Special Commissioner = **Rutherford**.

r: **Pedanandipadu firka**, Bapatla taluka, **Guntur** district – the no-tax campaign of Andhra
**Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary** – **"Andhra Shivaji"**; volunteer force **Shanti Sena**
Grievances of village officers; **18 of 19 village officers resigned** (led by Machiraju Ramamurthy); people refused **land revenue**
Gandhi advised suspension – suspended **11 Feb 1922**; ended by March 1922
Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri; **Nyapathi Subbarao** urged restraint
**T. Prakasam, Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Dantu Narayana Raju**
Revenue Board member **L.T. Harris** sent to Guntur; Rutherford's plan to ban the Shanti Sena rejected by the Madras Government
Decided upon by the **Guntur DCC in Dec 1921**; the campaign was suspended after Gandhi's message to Konda Venkatappayya reached the DCC
Tax on **grazing cattle in forest lands** (grass tax) – the "Forest Satyagraha", first in **Palnadu** (Guntur)
**Kanneganti Hanumanthu** – killed in police firing on **26 Feb 1922** (Minchalapadu)
Went to Palnadu in **July 1921** to study the agitation against the forest laws; arrested with Vedantam Narasimhachari

1.x: **Bezawada (Vijayawada) AICC, 31 March - 1 April 1921** brought Gandhi's programme into Andhra; **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)** let provinces start civil disobedience, including no-tax.

r: **"Ramadandu"** (1921) – Shanti Sena was Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary's (Pedanandipadu)
Met him in London (1915), introduced by **Ananda K. Coomaraswamy**
Founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** near Chirala (national education)
An Andhra secretary of the **Swaraj Party**
**Chirala and Perala**, Bapatla taluk, **Guntur** district – weavers and small farmers
The two villages were made a **municipality**; yearly tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000**
Met Duggirala at Vijayawada on **30 March 1921**, for the **Vijayawada AICC (31 March – 1 April 1921)**; visited Chirala on 6 April 1921
Midnight of **25 April 1921**: **13,572 of 15,326** residents left their homes
**Ram Nagar (Ramnagar)** outside municipal limits, with a parallel all-caste assembly (self-rule); Ramadandu built huts and dug wells; stay lasted **11 months**
After his speech at the Andhra Mahasabha, **Berhampur** (Sept-Oct 1921), for breaking a ban on speaking; tried by Rutherford at Srikakulam; one year's rigorous imprisonment
Lack of funds (the PCC did not grant even Rs 4,000), rivalry of Konda Venkatappayya and Pattabhi, no leader after his arrest
*Young India*: the municipality meant only more taxes and interference with liberty
Municipality abolished in **1938** by **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**, minister in the Rajaji ministry

2.x: Women: 12 arrested; **first woman jailed – Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**; Duvvuri Subbamma was also arrested.
Ramadandu = Duggirala = Chirala-Perala = Andhra Ratna; **Ram Nagar** = the township of the exodus.

r: **1921: visited Chittagong** and met Bengal revolutionaries (a British report)
Influenced by the NCM but believed in **force**; not a Congressman
Captured by Jamedar Kunchu Menon, shot at **Koyyur** on **7 May 1924** (Major Goodall)
Andhra Patrika (8 May 1924) hailed him as **a great national hero**

3.x: Memory: Agency district named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district**; 30-ft statue at **Bhimavaram** for his 125th birth anniversary; **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram** (Vizianagaram).
Born at **Mogallu** – shot at **Koyyur** – tomb at **Krishnadevipeta**.

r: Reserved forests cut podu (shifting cultivation), grazing and forest-produce rights

4.x: The Permanent Settlement played no part.

r: Against Mansabdar Madhava Bhupati; leaders Dwarabandala Chandrayya, Ambul Reddy; **Sullivan** removed Madhava Bhupati and the revolt was crushed in **Nov 1880**

Bhadrachalam taluk – rising against the **forest laws** and higher taxes on podu after the area joined the Madras Presidency (1874); spark – axe tax on podu raised from **4 annas to 4-12 annas** in a famine
Linked with both the Rampa and Rekapalli revolts

4.x: **Alluri** was born in 1897 – long after the 1879-80 revolt.

r: Vizianagaram – Vijayarama Raju killed at Padmanabham

4.x: Forest revolt of 1879 = **Rekapalli** (also given as Chinturu); Rampa 1922 = **Forest Act of 1882**.

r: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** (title given at the 1924 Andhra Mahasabha)
Wrote ***Bapu Blesses***; **Vahini** – a Telugu political journal linked with him and peasant leaders
Father of the **library movement** in Andhra
Novel ***Malapalli*** (written 1921 in Vellore jail, published 1922); ran **Sharada Niketan**, Guntur, with his wife Lakshmibayamma

5.x: Movements and leaders: Chirala-Perala – Duggirala; Palnadu – Kanneganti; Rampa – Alluri.
